description: Add clear, step-by-step user-facing instructions for running the PGRST205 fix, so the frustrated user has an unambiguous runbook. This can live as a top comment block inside supabase/FIX_PGRST205_permanent.sql AND/OR a short companion markdown note. The instructions must explain the diagnostic-first workflow, how to run the fix in the Supabase SQL Editor, what to expect, and the Dashboard fallback. Depends on FEAT-001 (the script must exist first).
steps: At the very top of supabase/FIX_PGRST205_permanent.sql (above the diagnostic section), add a header comment block titled 'HOW TO USE THIS FILE' with numbered steps: (1) Open Supabase Dashboard -> SQL Editor. (2) OPTIONAL but recommended: copy-run only Section A (diagnostics) first and note that campaigns has anon/authenticated grants while jobs/job_applications/banners do not - that difference IS the bug. (3) Copy the WHOLE file and Run it once. (4) Wait ~10 seconds for PostgREST to reload. (5) In the Flutter app, pull-to-refresh / reopen the Jobs and Banners screens - the PGRST205 error should be gone. (6) If it still fails, run the Section E verification queries and follow the Dashboard Exposed-schemas + Restart-project fallback.

State plainly in the header WHY previous attempts failed: rebuilding tables and NOTIFY/restart never ADDED the missing table-level GRANTs to the anon/authenticated roles, which is exactly what PostgREST needs; this script adds them.
Keep the instructions concise and in plain language (the user is stressed); avoid jargon where possible and do not use em dashes.
acceptance_criteria: supabase/FIX_PGRST205_permanent.sql begins with a 'HOW TO USE THIS FILE' numbered runbook covering: run diagnostics first, run the whole script, wait for reload, re-check the app, and the Dashboard fallback.
The header explains in one or two sentences why rebuilds + NOTIFY + restart did not fix it (missing GRANTs were never added).
No em dashes are used anywhere in the added text.
verification: Read the header of supabase/FIX_PGRST205_permanent.sql and confirm the numbered runbook and the 'why previous attempts failed' explanation are present.
grep the file for absence of the em dash character to confirm none were introduced.
findings: Added the 'HOW TO USE THIS FILE' header runbook at the very top of supabase/FIX_PGRST205_permanent.sql (above Section A). Numbered steps cover: open SQL Editor, optionally run Section A diagnostics first (campaigns has anon/authenticated grants while jobs/job_applications/banners do not - that difference is the bug), run the whole file once (idempotent), wait ~10s for PostgREST reload, pull-to-refresh/reopen Jobs and Banners screens, and the Section E verification + Dashboard Exposed-schemas/Restart-project fallback. Includes a 'WHY DID THE PREVIOUS ATTEMPTS NOT WORK?' paragraph explaining that rebuilds + NOTIFY + restart never ADDED the missing table-level GRANTs that PostgREST needs. Plain language, no jargon-heavy phrasing, and verified zero em dashes in the file.
